title: Bi-Continuous W-Rich Refractory High Entropy Alloy-Cu Composite: Toward Material Innovation of Nuclear Reactor Coolant System.

recollection.starting_material: Likely a refractory high entropy alloy (HEA) with tungsten (W) as a major component and copper (Cu).
recollection.intervention: Possibly a method to create a bi-continuous composite structure, such as liquid metal infiltration or co-casting.
recollection.structure: A bi-continuous composite with interconnected W-rich HEA and Cu phases.
recollection.mechanism: Likely involves phase separation or controlled solidification to achieve the bi-continuous structure.
recollection.results: Could include improved thermal conductivity, mechanical properties, and radiation resistance for nuclear reactor coolant applications.

score.note: The recollection does not identify liquid-metal dealloying in molten Cu at 1200 °C for 96 h. Its bicontinuous W-rich HEA/Cu description merely restates the title, while the proposed phase-separation/controlled-solidification mechanism is incorrect. No quantitative results are recalled.
